subsystems.name: Light absorber
subsystems.role: captures sunlight and creates the electrons and holes that drive the chemistry — the 'chlorophyll' of the device.
parts: tandem stacks (perovskite on silicon) to capture more of the spectrum

subsystems.name: Catalyst layers
subsystems.role: make the two half-reactions fast and selective so energy is not wasted.
parts: CO2-reduction catalyst (copper, silver, or molecular cobalt and manganese complexes)

subsystems.name: Membrane and electrolyte
subsystems.role: keeps the two half-reactions apart so their products cannot recombine.

subsystems.name: Product handling
subsystems.role: collects whatever comes off the cell: hydrogen, carbon monoxide, syngas or alcohols.

subsystems.name: Module and enclosure
subsystems.role: keeps water away from electrical contacts and wires many cells together into a panel.

buildSteps.title: Grow the light absorber
buildSteps.detail: Silicon wafers are doped and textured, or perovskite films are spin-coated or printed onto glass; a transparent conducting layer goes on top.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the catalysts
buildSteps.detail: Cobalt phosphate or manganese oxide is electrodeposited on the oxygen side; copper or silver is sputtered or plated on the side that will reduce CO2.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the membrane
buildSteps.detail: An ion-exchange or bipolar membrane is cut and conditioned to carry ions between the two half-cells while blocking crossover.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a single cell
buildSteps.detail: Absorber, catalysts and membrane are sandwiched together and the edges sealed with resin so only the catalyst touches the water.

buildSteps.title: Test under simulated sunlight
buildSteps.detail: The cell runs in a beaker under a solar simulator while the gas and liquid products are measured — this is where nearly all artificial-leaf work sits today.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a module
buildSteps.detail: Cells are stacked with shared manifolds feeding water in and taking gas and liquid products out.

buildSteps.title: Connect a CO2 feed
buildSteps.detail: Concentrated CO2 — from a flue gas stream or a capture unit — is fed to the cathode side.

buildSteps.title: Separate and purify the products
buildSteps.detail: Hydrogen and carbon monoxide are split by membranes; alcohols need distillation. Unreacted CO2 is recycled.

buildSteps.title: Prove the lifetime
buildSteps.detail: Cells must run for thousands of hours. Catalyst poisoning, membrane fouling and photoelectrode corrosion are the usual causes of failure.

prerequisites.why: silicon and perovskites work in air but corrode quickly when immersed and illuminated.
copper makes many products at once, so most of the current goes to hydrogen instead of fuel.
already mass-produced for fuel cells and water electrolysers.
capture from a power station or cement plant exists; direct air capture is far more expensive.
the leading designs avoid platinum and iridium, but long-term stability at low cost is unproven.

pathway.milestone: bench cells that split water into hydrogen, or reduce CO2 into syngas and small amounts of alcohols, at single-digit solar-to-fuel efficiency
pathway.unlocks: proof that sunlight can drive these reactions in one device. That is well below the roughly 10%+ achieved by a solar panel wired to an electrolyser.

pathway.milestone: devices using only abundant materials that run for thousands of hours without losing output
pathway.unlocks: a design worth engineering into a product rather than a paper.

pathway.milestone: pilot modules of a few square metres coupled to a real CO2 source
pathway.unlocks: real data on cost, fouling and maintenance.

pathway.milestone: plants making drop-in liquid fuels from captured CO2
pathway.unlocks: low-carbon fuel for aviation and shipping, where batteries are impractical. Note that burning the fuel returns the CO2 to the air, so this recycles carbon rather than storing it.
